summary: One long paragraph of the questioner's reply, mostly faithful and complete: the Kabbalistic terms (partzufim, sefirot, Ein Sof, the World of Emanation, the attribute) and the abbreviations (ז"א, א"א, מא"א as 'from Arikh Anpin', כס"א) follow the decisions, and מא"א is right. The main faults: איך נניח is 'leave aside' (as in 2:7), not 'posit'; לייטי עלה is 'they curse it', not 'there is none against it'; ענותך is 'your humility' (Ps 18:36); גדולים מהם is comparative; דמית has no object and is read as qal; ריש מלין אמר echoes Dan 7:1; the Isa 1:8 and Ps 100:3 notes misstate the verses and several allusions are not listed. Open: דחלות, ברותא, מהר"י.

patches.value: Reply from the questioner. My soul longed to hear words refined like cast mirrors, from the heights of heaven, burning. For I am poor in all knowledge, longing for the shade of the gourd. And instead of your humility making me great, you gave me to drink many waters, bitter as gall. You made me like a booth in a cucumber field, and my soul is incurable by praises of deceit (like the blessing of the wicked Balaam), dreadful ones. And with the words of a slanderer you concluded, and you resembled a man who casts off discipline, and a bereaved bear. And in truth this is not the way of the Torah. Our holy Torah, its ways are ways of pleasantness. And you shall love your neighbor as yourself. "What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow." Thus said Hillel, Prince of Israel! He stated the sum of the matter: as for my having opened my mouth to disparage the sages of Israel, and having brought out against them words that are not according to the law. Far be it from me to disparage any person, even a gentile, all the more so an Israelite. And I know no place in my words for what you claim, that there is disparagement in them. And if one raises difficulties against them from the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory, and reveals a place of contradiction, there is no prohibition in this at all. And also in the Talmud they raise difficulties even against those greater than they, and bring proof to refute their words, and say, "Refutation of Rabbi So-and-so." That of Rabbi So-and-so is a fabrication (the Arukh's reading: berota), and in Sanhedrin and in Berakhot we say: "The one who sees the rainbow must bow down, for it is written: 'Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud, etc., and I saw and fell on my face.'" "They curse it in the West, etc. Rabbi Abahu blasphemes against it, etc." And behold, in this your letter I found a complaint; a reply I did not find. Is it I who called these partzufim divinities? Did not the Kabbalists themselves say so. Go and learn from the intention of the blessings and the prayer: who is our God, and who is the God of our fathers. And in the Zohar he asks: "Who is this Elohim, such and such?" Moreover, for the Kabbalists explained that many worlds, thousands of thousands and myriads of myriads, were emanated, created, formed and made, only they did not put forth a hand to explain them because of their great concealment. For they are very subtle lights. And each world is comprised of ten sefirot. And each sefirah is comprised of ten details of details, as we said in the World of Emanation. And all of them are in the aspect of circles, this within this, and this inside that. And likewise in the aspect of the sefirot of straightness, which are in the form of a man of upright stature with 248 limbs, etc. All these worlds, each one of them comprises two aspects, of circles and of straightness, in general and in particular. And all the words of the Kabbalists and their explanations are only in the World of Emanation, which has already been coarsened and revealed more; and in it they explained all the matters of the comprehensive partzufim, which are five: Arikh Anpin, and Abba, and Imma, and Ze'ir, and his Nukva. Since it has already been made clear to you from their words that they say the partzufim were coarsened and revealed, and that they call the aforementioned partzufim divinities, when they say our God and the God of our fathers in prayer and in blessings, and that they intend a known attribute in every word. Your complaint does not stand against me, neither as a charge of corporeality nor as a charge of divinity, but against them, for they said it, and they said it. And the difficulty returns to its place: how shall we leave aside Ein Sof together with all the sefirot that are in the upper worlds, together with Arikh Anpin and Abba and Imma, and worship Ze'ir Anpin and say that He is our God, and we are His people and His servants; He made us, and to Him we are. In this letter of yours (where you said, "since it is known that the inner attributes are, some of them judgment and some of them mercy, etc.") you have already made a complete admission that this is your opinion: that no worship and no prayer applies to the Cause over all the causes, but only to Ze'ir Anpin, as the Rav Mikdash Melekh wrote, and Kisse Eliyahu, and Mahari Lopes in the Gate of the True Faith. Therefore we need you to resolve and answer for us how this opinion of the Kabbalists, that all our worship and our prayers are to Ze'ir Anpin and his soul, will agree with our holy Torah, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. And as for your anger that burned against me, and your saying that I ascribe corporeality to the sefirot, I also know no place for this in my words, for I said nothing that I did not find in their books. They said that the World of Emanation has in it a body, a soul and a garment. And it is not hidden from you that light, air and fire are subtle and light bodies. Moreover, they themselves explained their words, and said that the upper worlds and the partzufim above Arikh Anpin they did not speak of, only from Arikh Anpin and downward, since they had already been coarsened and revealed more. Behold, it is plain to you from their words that the sefirot they speak of were coarsened and revealed more than those above them, and they themselves admit that the sefirot they speak of were coarsened.
patches.reason: Several faults. (1) ענותך תרבני echoes Ps 18:36: ענות is 'humility, gentleness', not 'answer', and תרבני is 'would make me great', not 'enriching'. (2) איך נניח: הניח is 'leave aside', as the same question stands in 2:7 ('איך נניח שאר הפרצופים ונעבוד לזעיר אנפין'); 'posit' is wrong, and ונעבוד ונאמר belong to the same 'how' question, so the sentence must not split into a statement. (3) לייטי עלה is Aramaic 'they curse it' (participle of ל"ט), not 'there is none against it'. (4) גדולים מהם is 'greater than they', not 'the great among them'. (5) דמית has no object in the Hebrew: with ל it is the qal of דמה, 'you resembled' (Ezek 31:2), and פרוע מוסר is one phrase, 'one who casts off discipline' (Prov 13:18), so 'unrestrained man who casts off' counts פרוע twice. (6) ריש מלין אמר echoes Dan 7:1 (ראש מלין אמר, 'he told the sum of the matters'); it is not 'began his speech', and מה ש is 'as for my having ...', stating the charge of 2:7 ('פערת פיך', 'הוצאת עליהם דברים אשר לא כדת'). (7) ברותא is not 'baraita' (ברייתא); the variant is given as written. (8) דחלות is Aramaic 'fearsome', fem. pl., agreeing with תהלות: 'dreadful ones' (see the token note and question). (9) שלחו יד is 'put forth a hand'. (10) במכתבך זה: 'this' was dropped. (11) הרב מקדש מלך: the Rav is named by his book; 'of' made it a place. Nothing else in the English is changed.

patches.reason: The literal line omitted 'not' in שלא שלחו, and carried the glosses corrected in the English (ענותך, דחלות, דמית, ריש מלין אמר, גדולים מהם, ברותא, לייטי עלה, נניח).
ענות is 'humility, gentleness' (Ps 18:36 'ענותך תרבני'), not 'answer' (that would be תשובה or מענה).

patches.value: ענותך: 'your humility'; the phrase is Ps 18:36, said of God's gentleness. Here it is ironic: the respondent's humility was to make the questioner great. Another reading, 'your answering', is in `readings`.
patches.reason: A learner needs the allusion.
תרבני is from רבה, 'make great, increase' (Ps 18:36); 'enrich' is not in the verb.

דחלות is Aramaic (root דחל, 'fear'), feminine plural, so it agrees with תהלות and describes the praises; 'fearful' read as the soul's state is the less natural parse. The word is a hapax in this book (grep of the corpus finds no other use).

patches.value: דחלות: Aramaic 'fearsome, dreaded' (דחיל; cf. דחילו in the Zohar's 'fear and love'), feminine plural in agreement with תהלות: 'deceitful praises, dreadful ones'. The author's Balaam parenthesis stands between the two. The word דחלא also means 'idol' in the Targums, and the translator's 'fearful' (the soul afraid) is a possible reading: see `readings`. Proposed ruling in the decisions.
patches.reason: A guessed Aramaic word needs its note and the open alternatives.
פרוע מוסר is one phrase (Prov 13:18 פורע מוסר): 'one who casts off discipline'; 'unrestrained' plus 'casting off' counted פרוע twice.
With 46, the phrase 'casting off discipline'.

דמית with ל and no object is the qal of דמה, 'you were like' (Ezek 31:2, 18 'אל מי דמית'). The translator's 'you likened' needs an object the Hebrew does not write, and the English was left without one.

patches.value: דמית: read as qal 'you were like' (cf. Ezek 31:2), the ל of ולאיש governing both nouns. If it is piel, 'you likened (me)', the Hebrew writes no object: see `readings`.
patches.reason: A learner needs the parse.

patches.value: ריש מלין אמר is Aramaic and echoes Dan 7:1 (ראש מלין אמר, 'he told the sum of the matters'): 'He stated the sum of the matter'. It introduces the questioner's restatement of the respondent's charge (2:7 'פערת פיך ... הוצאת עליהם דברים אשר לא כדת'). It does not mean 'began his speech'.
patches.reason: Proposed ruling: render a Dan 7:1 echo by the verse's sense; the subject of אמר is the respondent, whose charge follows.
גדולים מהם is comparative: 'greater than they', not 'the great among them'.
The מ of מהם is comparative.
ברותא is the Arukh's variant spelling of בדותא; it is not ברייתא, so 'baraita' is a guess. The meaning is not given in the text.

patches.value: ברותא: the variant, kept as written. 'Baraita' would be ברייתא, a different word.
patches.reason: Proposed ruling: a variant spelling that the text does not gloss is transliterated, with a note, and not translated.
לייטי is the Aramaic masculine plural participle of ל"ט, 'curse', not 'there is none'.
עלה is Aramaic 'on it, over it'; with לייטי, 'they curse it'.

patches.value: Aramaic (Bavli): לייטי עלה במערבא 'they curse it in the West' (the West is the Land of Israel); מגדף בה, 'blasphemes against it'.
patches.reason: Learner note.
שלא is 'that ... not'; the gloss dropped the negation.
שלחו יד is 'put forth a hand'.
הניח is 'leave aside, abandon', as in 2:7 (איך נניח שאר הפרצופים ונעבוד לזעיר אנפין); 'posit' is not the sense.

patches.value: נניח: from הניח, 'leave aside'. The verbs ונעבוד and ונאמר depend on the same 'how': 'how shall we leave Ein Sof aside, and worship Ze'ir Anpin and say ...'.
patches.reason: Learner note.

patches.value: הרב מקדש מלך: the Rav is called by the title of his book (Mikdash Melekh, 'Temple of the King', a commentary on the Zohar); the text gives no name.
patches.reason: The English now reads 'the Rav Mikdash Melekh', as written; a note says who is meant.

patches.value: מהר"י: an acronym, 'morenu ha-Rav Rabbi Y...', the Y being the initial of the first name, which the text does not give. The same acronym is used of Albo, Tzahari and others in the book.
patches.reason: The existing note drops the Y.

value: The paragraph is the questioner's reply in chapter 2 (תשובה מהשואל): 'I' is the questioner and 'you' is the respondent, who is addressed throughout.
In 'איותה נפשי לשמוע', the soul is the subject of the verb of longing and the infinitive is its object; 'מוזקקות' and 'מוצקות' agree with 'אמרות' (words).

'ובדברי נרגן סיימת ... דמית': the verbs have no object written. 'דמית' with ל is read as qal, 'you resembled' (Ezek 31:2); read as piel it would be 'you likened (me)'. 'פרוע מוסר' is one phrase, 'one who casts off discipline' (Prov 13:18).

Aramaic (Bavli): 'מה דעלך סני לחברך' is Hillel's saying; 'הא דר' פלוני בדותא היא' and 'לייטי עלה במערבא ... מגדף בה' ('they curse it in the West ... he blasphemes against it') are Talmudic Aramaic. 'מאן אלהים דא כך וכך' is Zohar Aramaic. 'אמרינן' ('we say') introduces the Talmudic statement.
'ריש מלין אמר' is Aramaic and echoes Dan 7:1 (ראש מלין אמר): 'he stated the sum of the matter'. What follows, 'מה שאני פערתי פי ...', restates the respondent's charge of 2:7.

'איך נניח האין סוף ... ונעבוד לז"א ונאמר' is one question: הניח is 'leave aside', and ונעבוד ונאמר are the second and third verbs under the same 'how' ('how shall we leave Ein Sof aside, and worship Ze'ir Anpin and say ...').
patches.reason: The note on ריש מלין as an idiom 'began his speech' was wrong; the note on the missing object is replaced by the parse; the Aramaic note now covers לייטי עלה; the question of איך נניח is explained.

value: The unit has no marked Wikisource additions; the 1931 scan has not been collated (decisions, Q2).
Job 37:18 (embedded allusion): 'like cast mirrors' (כראי מוצקות), from 'like a cast mirror'. Ps 12:7 (echo): 'refined' (מוזקקות) of words.
Job 7:2 (embedded): 'longing for the shade' (שואף לצל). Jonah 4:6 (allusion): 'the gourd' (הקיקיון).
Ps 18:36 (embedded): 'ענותך תרבני', 'your humility has made me great', turned to irony.
Isa 1:8 (embedded): the verse reads 'like a hut in a vineyard, like a lodge in a cucumber field' (כסוכה בכרם כמלונה במקשה). The author takes the second clause (כמלונה במקשה) alone.
Hos 13:8 and Prov 17:12 (embedded): 'a bereaved bear' (דוב שכול). Prov 13:18 (embedded): 'one who casts off discipline' (פורע מוסר). Prov 18:8 (embedded): 'the words of a slanderer' (דברי נרגן).
Prov 3:17 (embedded): 'its ways are ways of pleasantness' (דרכיה דרכי נועם; the verse reads 'דרכיה דרכי נעם').
Lev 19:18: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself' (ואהבת לרעך כמוך).
Dan 7:1 (echo): 'ריש מלין אמר', from 'ראש מלין אמר', 'he told the sum of the matters'. Esth 4:16 (echo): 'not according to the law' (אשר לא כדת).
Ezek 1:28 (quoted in part): 'like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud' and 'I saw and fell on my face' (ואראה ואפול על פני).

Ps 100:3 (embedded): 'He made us, and to Him we are' (הוא עשנו ולו אנחנו). The verse's ketiv is 'ולא אנחנו' and its qere 'ולו אנחנו'; the author writes the qere. 'His people and His servants' (עמו ועבדיו) replaces the verse's 'and the flock of His pasture'; the English follows the author's wording.
The saying 'What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow' is attributed to Hillel by the author, who gives no reference.
בדותא / ברותא: the printed text reads בדותא ('fabrication'); the note in parentheses gives the Arukh's reading ברותא, which the English leaves transliterated (berota).
מא"א (2:8.521) is read as מאריך אנפין, from the same sentence ('שלמעלה מאריך אנפין ... רק מא"א ולמטה'); the reading is certain.
דחלות (2:8.41): read as 'dreadful ones', agreeing with תהלות; the alternative, 'fearful' (the soul afraid), is in `readings`.
patches.reason: The Isa 1:8 line misquoted the verse (the verse has כמלונה במקשה); the Ps 100:3 line described the ketiv as the verse's wording and the qere as the author's departure; Prov 3:17, Prov 18:8, Prov 13:18, Ps 18:36, Job 7:2, Dan 7:1 and Esth 4:16 were not listed; the Arukh line said the English follows the printed text but the note gave 'baraita'.

value.english: and you likened me to a man who casts off discipline, and to a bereaved bear
value.note: Reads דמית as piel, 'you likened', with an object (me) understood; the Hebrew writes none.

value.english: fearful (the soul afraid)
value.note: Reads דחלות as describing the soul, not the praises; an Aramaic word for 'idols' (דחלא) is a further possibility that the context does not support.

value.english: your answering would increase me
value.note: Reads ענותך as 'your answering'; the allusion to Ps 18:36 (ענותך תרבני) favours 'your humility'.

patches.reason: The translator listed no alternatives. Proposed list; each is a real grammatical or lexical possibility.
